title: Goal and events: user controls and durable execution boundaries
description: Goal, 目标、事件驱动 and 子agent progress: user controls, durable execution facts and the approvals needed for effects.
body:
Goal is a user-controlled long-running workflow. The DAC Session UI provides its existing start, pause, resume and plan-edit controls; use the displayed phase, revision and permission checks. This manual does not introduce goal_* or event_* model tools. A normal plan tool edits the session work plan and is not authority to start or resume a Goal.

Read task progress from the current task/Goal surfaces. Child-agent work is inspectable through task_status/task_read for tasks this Session owns; the parent receives their results. A UI progress card is a read view, not permission to send arbitrary instructions to other users’ agents. Unknown or recovery_required work needs its existing explicit recovery path; do not replace it with a new task or replay a provider effect.

EventV2 durably records admission, execution state, checkpoints and outbox delivery so GUI/TUI and background work can observe the same facts. Durable prompt admission is separate from model execution; it does not itself prove a model call or side effect completed. Current consumers must retain their domain idempotency or execution owner. A completed receipt may deduplicate delivery; pending/unknown is not universal exactly-once authority. Event investigation uses its existing UI/MCP/permission boundaries. An event description or diagnostic finding never authorizes a mutation, new model run or remote action.
